q: Fill up: Preterm labour is defined as labour beginning at ______ weeks.
Fill up: The most common cause of preterm labour is ______ and an iatrogenic example is ______.
opts: idiopathic; induction at 34 weeks in severe pre-eclampsia
induction at 34 weeks in severe pre-eclampsia; idiopathic
infection; induction at 40 weeks at term
polyhydramnios; elective caesarean at 37 weeks

q: Which of the following statements about risk factors for preterm labour is TRUE?
opts: Previous history of preterm labour is the most important risk factor for preterm birth
Short cervix alone is the most important risk factor, more than previous preterm birth
PROM is the most important risk factor for preterm labour in all populations
Twin pregnancy is the most important risk factor for preterm labour worldwide

q: All of the following cause uterine overdistension leading to preterm labour EXCEPT:
opts: Twins and polyhydramnios causing uterine overdistension and preterm contractions
Fibroids and adenomyosis causing uterine overdistension and preterm labour
Oligohydramnios causing uterine overdistension and preterm contractions
Cervical polyps causing uterine overdistension and leading to preterm labour

q: Fill up: Bleeding in pregnancy causing preterm labour is most commonly due to ______.
opts: abruptio placenta
placenta previa
vasa previa
cervical ectropion

q: Match the stress contributor with its example — 1) Maternal stress 2) Fetal stress … A) PIH B) Uteroplacental insufficiency and IUGR
All of the following maternal infections are linked to preterm labour with no routine screening advised EXCEPT:
opts: Asymptomatic bacteriuria and bacterial vaginosis, neither routinely screened for PTL prevention
Syphilis and HIV infection, neither routinely screened for PTL prevention in low-risk women
Tuberculosis and malaria, neither routinely screened for preterm labour prevention
Chlamydia and gonorrhoea, neither routinely screened for preterm labour prevention

q: A 26-year-old woman with previous preterm birth at 32 weeks is now 18 weeks. She asks if her risk can be predicted. Which patients have preventable preterm labour and what is the IOC tool for prediction?
opts: Previous preterm birth or short cervix; transvaginal sonography is the investigation of choice
All primigravid women screened by transabdominal sonography for cervical length routinely
Twin pregnancies alone screened by magnetic resonance imaging for cervical length
Preterm prelabour rupture alone monitored with cardiotocography for contractions

q: Fill up: A short cervix on TVS risking preterm labour is defined as ______ cm or less.
Fill up: As cervix dilates in preterm labour, its T shape changes in sequence ______.
opts: T → Y → V → U
T → V → Y → U
U → V → Y → T
Y → T → V → U

q: Fill up: ACOG recommends cervical length measurement by TVS between ______ weeks in women with history of PTL.
Which of the following statements about TVS cervical length measurement precautions is TRUE?
opts: Measure with empty bladder from internal os to external os for cervical length assessment
Measure with full bladder and measure only the visible part of cervix on TVS
Measure with full bladder from external os to internal os with fundal pressure
Measure without bladder preparation and include lower uterine segment in length

q: All of the following lifestyle measures help prevent preterm labour EXCEPT:
opts: Quit smoking as a preventive measure for preterm labour in at-risk women
Strict bed rest as a proven preventive measure for preterm labour
Treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria when detected in antenatal screening
Progesterone prophylaxis in women with previous preterm birth or short cervix

q: A 29-year-old woman with previous preterm birth at 30 weeks, singleton pregnancy, TVS cervix 2.0 cm at 18 weeks. She asks about cerclage. Which three indications are required for cervical cerclage surgery?
opts: Preterm birth history, cervical length 2.5 cm or less on TVS, singleton pregnancy
Preterm labour history, twin pregnancy and short cervix on transabdominal scan
Previous term delivery, cervical length 3.5 cm and singleton pregnancy at 20 weeks
No previous preterm birth but short cervix alone in twin pregnancy at 16 weeks

q: Fill up: Cervical cerclage timing is ______ weeks with ______ given alongside.
opts: 14–24; progesterone
10–12; antibiotics
24–28; tocolytics
28–32; steroids

q: All of the following are indications for progesterone prophylaxis of preterm labour EXCEPT:
opts: Previous preterm birth, cervical length ≤25 mm and adjunct to cervical cerclage as per notes
Twin pregnancy alone whatever the cervical length or obstetric history without other risk
Singleton pregnancy with short cervix on TVS between 16 and 24 weeks gestation
History-indicated cerclage with progesterone as adjunct therapy for prevention

q: Match progesterone regimen with its details — 1) Hydroxyprogesterone caproate 2) Micronised progesterone … A) IM weekly 16-20 to 36 weeks B) PV daily
Which of the following statements about progesterone mechanism in PTL prevention is TRUE?
opts: Progesterone prevents preterm labour by acting as a smooth muscle relaxant maintaining quiescence
Progesterone acts as a tocolytic after contractions have started to stop established labour
Progesterone prevents preterm labour by increasing oxytocin receptor expression in myometrium
Progesterone prevents preterm labour by ripening the cervix and increasing gap junctions

q: Which of the following statements about progesterone as tocolytic is TRUE?
opts: Progesterone is not a tocolytic and cannot stop labour once contractions have started
Progesterone is the first-line tocolytic agent in established preterm labour
Progesterone stops contractions within 30 minutes when given intravenously in labour
Progesterone is more effective than nifedipine for acute tocolysis in preterm labour

q: All of the following have NO role in preventing preterm labour EXCEPT:
opts: Bed rest, nutrient supplementation and routine screening for infection have no role in PTL prevention
Progesterone and cerclage have no role in preventing preterm labour in at-risk women
Smoking cessation has no role in preventing preterm labour and can be ignored
Transvaginal cervical length screening has no role in predicting preterm labour

q: Fill up: Established preterm labour is defined as regular contractions with cervical dilatation ≥______ cm and effacement ≥______%.
Which of the following statements about fetal fibronectin in PTL is TRUE?
opts: Fetal fibronectin is a glycoprotein from choriodecidual interface predicting preterm labour
Fetal fibronectin is a hormone from corpus luteum maintaining pregnancy until term
Fetal fibronectin is a fetal lung maturity marker measured in amniotic fluid routinely
Fetal fibronectin is a maternal serum marker for Down syndrome screening in twins

q: A 30-year-old woman at 32 weeks with regular contractions, cervix 2 cm dilated, 80% effaced, membranes intact, no bleeding. Fetal fibronectin is positive. What is the diagnosis and best predictor?
opts: Established preterm labour; fetal fibronectin positive predicts delivery within 7-14 days
False labour; fetal fibronectin positive rules out preterm labour completely
Term labour; fetal fibronectin is irrelevant after 37 weeks gestation
Braxton Hicks contractions; no need for steroids or tocolysis at 32 weeks

q: Match intervention in established PTL with its purpose — 1) Corticosteroids 2) Tocolytics 3) MgSO4 4) Antibiotics … A) Fetal lung maturity B) Delay delivery 48h C) Neuroprotection D) GBS prophylaxis
Fill up: In established PTL, steroids are given as ______ IM 12 hours apart or ______ IM 24 hours apart.
opts: betamethasone; dexamethasone
dexamethasone; betamethasone
hydrocortisone; betamethasone
prednisolone; dexamethasone
